logline: Just before closing, a young woman hands an elderly bookshop owner a faded letter from her grandmother, and as he reads its first line he slowly removes his glasses, overwhelmed by a past he thought was buried.

setting.place: A quiet independent bookshop, at the checkout counter

characters.name: Arthur Penhale
characters.role: the old bookshop owner receiving the letter

assumptions.value: A quiet independent bookshop, at the checkout counter
Clara Whitmore, a young woman aged 24, the granddaughter delivering the letter
Arthur Penhale, the old shop owner aged 74
A faded letter slid across the counter
He reads the first line and slowly takes off his glasses
Clara speaks the locked line; Arthur stays silent, reacting only through action
14 seconds: one spoken line of about 5 seconds plus time for the letter slide, the reading and the glasses moment

locked_lines: My grandmother asked me to give you this. She said you would understand.
